To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multitude of questions teachers have during teaching cannot be answered with current research tools.
learning analytics tools need to support the following aspects: (a) usability of the tool; (b) the functionality of the tool; and (c) the impact of the tool on teaching and learning.
the current state of research in learning analytics does not yet allow to answer the multitude of questions of teachers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Which questions do teachers ask in their teaching practice and which indicators could be useful to answer these questions?

how the multitude of research questions can be systematically mapped to sets of research indicators and how the effects of research indicators can be evaluated in order to support teachers in technology-enhanced teaching.
the following questions: Which indicators should learning analytics tools provide?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is still much room for research on how learning analytics can support teaching.
learning analytics should not be considered as a separate research discipline, but rather as a methodological approach that can be applied in many disciplines.
learning analytics should be more usable, more useful, and have a greater impact on learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning analytics is not yet ready for use in action research, but that it has the potential for this.
learning analytics is not yet ready for use by teachers in the classroom.
there are many questions that are not yet answered by learning analytics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field of learning analytics is still young, and there is much potential in the development of tools that support teachers and students in the learning process.
learning analytics should be designed for supporting the teachers' decision making in their teaching.
learning analytics can be a powerful means to support action research, if the research questions are mapped to sets of appropriate indicators.
